title: Border blockade and supply shortages in Nepal
summary: Madhesi protesters opposed to Nepal's new constitution blocked the main Birgunj border crossing, causing severe fuel and medicine shortages; Nepal accused India of an unofficial blockade, which India denied, citing the unrest. The border reopened in February 2016 after constitutional amendments.

summary: The first regional cross-border petroleum pipeline, 41 km from Raxaul/Motihari to Amlekhgunj, was inaugurated; it was funded and built by Indian Oil Corporation.

title: Kalapani-Lipulekh map dispute
summary: After India inaugurated a road to Lipulekh, Nepal published a revised map showing Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura as Nepali territory; its lower house approved the map on 13 June 2020. India rejected the map as a unilateral act not based on historical facts or evidence.

summary: During Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal's visit to New Delhi, the revised Treaty of Transit was signed and the two sides announced a long-term power trade agreement for India to import 10,000 MW from Nepal within ten years.

title: Nepal power to Bangladesh through Indian grid
summary: Under a trilateral agreement signed in October 2024, power trade from Nepal to Bangladesh via India's grid was inaugurated; actual transmission of 40 MW began on 15 June 2025.

summary: After armed tribesmen from Pakistan's North-West Frontier Province entered Jammu and Kashmir, Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India on 26 October 1947 and Indian troops were sent in. The fighting ended in a UN-supervised ceasefire; the first UN military observers arrived in January 1949.

India began air operations on 26 May and on 12 July 1999 announced that Operation Vijay had succeeded and the Line of Control was being restored.

summary: India's Director General of Military Operations announced that the Army had struck militant launch pads across the Line of Control. Pakistan's military denied that such strikes took place and described the incident as cross-border fire.
